raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Qwen3CoderDetector.parse_streaming_increment()` still buffers an entire open string parameter on upstream main `fb6e6a09ce5e3dc2ebc93ee64d11572a4da4d758` (2026-10-21). Long file-writing arguments can therefore leave an agent client without tool-argument deltas for minutes while decoding continues.

This updates the existing PR against that main commit and addresses the compatibility concerns discussed in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25246#issuecomment-6308754839. It changes parser delivery, not model outputs, decoding, scheduling, or tool execution.

## Changes

- Incrementally emit declared parameters whose existing `_get_param_type()` conversion is string-like. Reuse the upstream helper rather than introducing a conflicting method or a second schema interpretation. This includes nullable/composed string schemas and existing string aliases. Declared untyped parameters use the existing string fallback; undeclared parameters retain the complete-value path.
- Preserve the complete-value path for arrays (including `anyOf` arrays), objects, integers and booleans.
- Preserve case-insensitive literal `null` conversion, one leading/trailing LF removal, JSON escaping, and split parameter/function terminators.
- Retain a bounded suffix rather than the entire open string, and do not synthesize closing syntax for interrupted output.
- Extend the existing Qwen3 Coder tests with composed schemas, non-string conversions, consecutive leading newlines, split terminators, and consecutive tool calls.

## Validation on the updated code

- CPU-only environment, with upstream-pinned `transformers==5.19.0` and `xgrammar==0.2.7`.
- All 23 `TestQwen3CoderDetector` methods pass, including structural-tag checks and 335 parameterized equivalence/typing/terminator subcases across four tests. The isolated class runner executes the unchanged upstream test class with real detector, protocol, schema utilities, and xgrammar; only unrelated package bootstrap/test imports are avoided.
- Negative control: the same tests against the unmodified main detector report 44 failures (including subtest failures), detecting missing incremental delivery and unbounded open-value buffering.
- 20 CPU adapter replays pass: actual detector fragments are serialized with the OpenAI streaming protocol and passed through the current Anthropic stream converter. Long string arguments arrive before the parameter closes; concatenated OpenAI/Anthropic arguments match non-streaming parsing. This uses a synthetic backend stream and replaces only the telemetry-clock import with `time.monotonic`; it is not a live HTTP/GPU test.
- Ruff selected upstream lint rules, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` pass.

The full test-module import is blocked locally by the CPU environment lacking Triton. Full maintainer CI remains required. This revision has not been deployed to a GPU service and does not claim an inference speedup.

## Historical physical evidence (original September revision, not rerun for this update)

A paired single-request replay used the same model, weights, prompt, tool schema, and generated 15,375-character `content`; only the detector changed:

| Measurement | Existing detector | Original patched detector |
|---|---:|---:|
| SSE events | 8 | 2,108 |
| Longest silence from request start | 300.893 s | 16.058 s |
| Longest gap after streaming began | 300.893 s | 0.421 s |
| Final tool arguments / content SHA-256 | identical | identical |

Request completion was 317.40 s versus 313.04 s; this was not claimed as a speedup. The purpose is progressive delivery with compatible final arguments and bounded parser buffering.

Related: #27005, #25246.

Local parser regression checks (125 cases plus interruption/bounded-buffer coverage) and the paired physical-service evidence are documented in the PR body. Could a maintainer please add the `run-ci` label when appropriate? Thank you.

Tested the detector changes from #41313 against sglang v0.5.22 (`qwen3_coder_detector`) using @hanxiao's `test_stream.py` from the comment on #25246: 8 calls at each chunk size of 1, 2, 3, 5, 17, and 4096. The detector hunks apply with small offsets; I did not apply the PR's test-file hunk.

- Stock v0.5.22: 1 failure (string argument not emitted before `</parameter>`)
- With #41313: 0 failures in this suite
- With #25246 instead, for comparison: every non-string parameter raises `TypeError: _get_param_type() missing 1 required positional argument: 'param_config'`

These were parser-level tests on CPU only. I have not yet run an end-to-end streaming request with #41313 on v0.5.22.

> PR title must use "[Type] scope: title" or "[Type] [Hardware] scope: title". Type must be one of: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, Chore. Scope is required and may be any module or model name, with unrestricted letter case (letters, numbers, dots, underscores, slashes, or hyphens). Hardware is optional; use a single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend. Reverts must use GitHub's default format: Revert "original title". Use one space between fields and after the colon, with a non-empty title and no leading or trailing whitespace. Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
Edit the title; the check reruns on its own.

Update on the latest revision (`b239e3d6`, replacing `732e852`):

- Rebased onto upstream main snapshot `fb6e6a09`.
- Expanded incremental string-argument delivery beyond explicit `type: string` schemas by reusing the existing `_get_param_type()` helper. Nullable/composed string schemas, existing string aliases, and declared untyped parameters now follow the existing string conversion semantics. Undeclared parameters and non-string values retain the complete-value path.
- Added regression coverage for composed schemas, array/non-string conversion, consecutive leading newlines, split terminators, and consecutive tool calls.

The original implementation already provided incremental delivery, bounded suffix buffering, literal `null` handling, and interruption handling without synthesizing closing syntax. This revision extends compatibility and validation rather than changing those goals.

Validation of this revision: all 23 detector test methods pass in the isolated CPU class runner, including 335 subcases across four tests; 20 CPU OpenAI-to-Anthropic adapter replays pass; selected Ruff checks, formatting, and diff checks pass. The same detector tests against unmodified main produce 44 failures (including subtest failures), demonstrating coverage of the original buffering issue. These checks do not replace full upstream CI or live GPU end-to-end validation. The full test-module import was blocked locally by missing Triton.

Thanks @pos-ei-don for independently testing the earlier revision on v0.5.22. That result is useful compatibility evidence; it should not be interpreted as a test of this newer commit.

The PR title has also been corrected to the current convention, and the latest title check passes. Other CI gates remain unresolved; I am not claiming that the full CI suite is green. Maintainer guidance on enabling the appropriate CI would be appreciated.

Thanks for the update. I re-ran @hanxiao's `test_stream.py` suite on sglang v0.5.22 with the `qwen3_coder_detector` patch from `b239e3d6` applied cleanly (PR test-file hunk not applied): 8 calls × chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 5, 17, and 4096, with streaming output matching `detect_and_parse`. Zero failures, as with `732e852`. CPU parser-level testing only; no end-to-end streaming request tested yet.

@@ -57,6 +57,7 @@ def __init__(self):
 
         # Initialize attributes that were missing in the original PR
         self.current_func_name: Optional[str] = None
+        self._stream_string: Optional[dict] = None
 
     def has_tool_call(self, text: str) -> bool:
         return self.tool_call_start_token in text
@@ -243,6 +244,79 @@ def detect_and_parse(self, text: str, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult
             logger.error(f"Error in detect_and_parse: {e}")
             return StreamingParseResult(normal_text=text)
 
+    def _emit_string_parameter(self, calls: List[ToolCallItem]) -> bool:
+        """Emit safe string prefixes while retaining possible delimiters."""
+        state = self._stream_string
+        value = self._buffer[self.parsed_pos :]
+        if state["leading"] and value:
+            state["leading"] = False
+            if value.startswith("\n"):
+                self.parsed_pos += 1
+                value = value[1:]
+
+        ends = [
+            (value.find(tag), consume)
+            for tag, consume in (
+                (self.parameter_end_token, len(self.parameter_end_token)),
+                (self.parameter_prefix, 0),
+                (self.function_end_token, 0),
+            )
+        ]
+        ends = [(pos, consume) for pos, consume in ends if pos >= 0]
+        complete = bool(ends)
+        if complete:
+            end, consume = min(ends)
+            chunk = value[:end]
+            if chunk.endswith("\n"):
+                chunk = chunk[:-1]
+            advance = end + consume
+        else:
+            # Retain a possible literal null, final LF, and delimiter prefix.
+            keep = max(
+                map(
+                    len,
+                    (
+                        self.parameter_end_token,
+                        self.parameter_prefix,
+                        self.function_end_token,
+                    ),
+                )
+            ) + len("null")
+            advance = max(0, len(value) - keep)
+            if not advance:
+                return False
+            chunk = value[:advance]
+
+        fragment = ""
+        if not state["opened"]:
+            if not self.json_started:
+                fragment += "{"
+                self.json_started = True
+            if self.current_tool_param_count:
+                fragment += ", "
+            fragment += json.dumps(state["name"]) + ": "
+            if complete and chunk.lower() == "null":
+                fragment += "null"
+            else:
+                fragment += '"' + json.dumps(chunk, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1]
+                if complete:
+                    fragment += '"'
+            state["opened"] = True
+        else:
+            fragment += json.dumps(chunk, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1]
+            if complete:
+                fragment += '"'
+
+        if fragment:
+            calls.append(
+                ToolCallItem(tool_index=self.current_tool_id, parameters=fragment)
+            )
+        self.parsed_pos += advance
+        if complete:
+            self.current_tool_param_count += 1
+            self._stream_string = None
+        return complete
+
     def parse_streaming_increment(
         self, new_text: str, tools: List[Tool]
     ) -> StreamingParseResult:
@@ -259,6 +333,11 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
         normal_text_chunks = []
 
         while True:
+            if self._stream_string is not None:
+                if self._emit_string_parameter(calls):
+                    continue
+                break
+
             # Working text slice
             current_slice = self._buffer[self.parsed_pos :]
 
@@ -308,6 +387,29 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
             if current_slice.startswith(self.parameter_prefix):
                 name_end = current_slice.find(">")
                 if name_end != -1:
+                    param_name = current_slice[len(self.parameter_prefix) : name_end]
+                    param_config = self._get_arguments_config(
+                        self.current_func_name, tools
+                    )
+                    schema = param_config.get(param_name)
+                    # Match complete-value conversion, including nullable and
+                    # composed schemas. Undeclared parameters keep the old path.
+                    if param_name in param_config and self._get_param_type(schema) in (
+                        "string",
+                        "str",
+                        "text",
+                        "varchar",
+                        "char",
+                        "enum",
+                    ):
+                        self._stream_string = {
+                            "name": param_name,
+                            "opened": False,
+                            "leading": True,
+                        }
+                        self.parsed_pos += name_end + 1
+                        continue
+
                     value_start_idx = name_end + 1
                     rest_of_slice = current_slice[value_start_idx:]

@@ -2368,6 +2368,21 @@ def setUp(self):
                     },
                 ),
             ),
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="write_file",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {
+                            "file_path": {"type": "string"},
+                            "content": {"type": "string"},
+                            "count": {"type": "integer"},
+                            "metadata": {"type": "object"},
+                        },
+                    },
+                ),
+            ),
         ]
         self.detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
 
@@ -2477,6 +2492,237 @@ def test_streaming_single_tool_call(self):
             self.assertEqual(params["location"], "Boston")
             self.assertEqual(params["unit"], "celsius")
 
+    def test_streaming_string_parameter_emits_before_closing_tag(self):
+        detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
+        prefix = (
+            "<tool_call><function=write_file>"
+            "<parameter=file_path>/tmp/demo</parameter>"
+            "<parameter=content>"
+        )
+        calls = detector.parse_streaming_increment(prefix, self.tools).calls
+        calls += detector.parse_streaming_increment("x" * 1000, self.tools).calls
+
+        fragments = "".join(call.parameters for call in calls)
+        self.assertIn('"content": "', fragments)
+        self.assertIn("x" * 100, fragments)
+        self.assertLess(len(detector._buffer), 128)
+
+        tail = (
+            "</parameter><parameter=count>42</parameter>"
+            '<parameter=metadata>{"a": [1, 2]}</parameter>'
+            "</function></tool_call>"
+        )
+        calls += detector.parse_streaming_increment(tail, self.tools).calls
+        parameters = "".join(call.parameters for call in calls)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            json.loads(parameters),
+            {
+                "file_path": "/tmp/demo",
+                "content": "x" * 1000,
+                "count": 42,
+                "metadata": {"a": [1, 2]},
+            },
+        )
+
+    def test_streaming_string_parameter_matches_non_streaming(self):
+        values = [
+            "",
+            "null",
+            "NULL",
+            "nul",
+            "nullish",
+            "\n",
+            "\n\n",
+            "\n hello\n",
+            "\n\nbody\n",
+            '中文🙂"\\\t\r\n' * 20,
+            "a < x and </param is not a delimiter",
+        ]
+        for value in values:
+            text = (
+                "<tool_call><function=write_file>"
+                "<parameter=file_path>/tmp/demo</parameter>"
+                f"<parameter=content>{value}</parameter>"
+                "<parameter=count>42</parameter>"
+                '<parameter=metadata>{"a": [1, 2]}</parameter>'
+                "</function></tool_call>"
+            )
+            expected = json.loads(
+                Qwen3CoderDetector()
+                .detect_and_parse(text, self.tools)
+                .calls[0]
+                .parameters
+            )
+            for chunk_size in (1, 2, 3, 5, 17, 41, len(text)):
+                with self.subTest(value=value, chunk_size=chunk_size):
+                    detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
+                    fragments = []
+                    for offset in range(0, len(text), chunk_size):
+                        result = detector.parse_streaming_increment(
+                            text[offset : offset + chunk_size], self.tools
+                        )
+                        fragments.extend(call.parameters for call in result.calls)
+                    self.assertEqual(json.loads("".join(fragments)), expected)
+
+    def test_streaming_composed_string_schemas_emit_before_closing_tag(self):
+        """String unions must not buffer the whole value or change conversion."""
+        schemas = [
+            {"type": ["string", "null"]},
+            {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]},
+            {"oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"type": "string"}]},
+            {"allOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"maxLength": 4096}]},
+            {"enum": ["hello", "world"]},
+            {"type": "str"},
+            {},
+        ]
+        for schema in schemas:
+            tools = [
+                Tool(
+                    type="function",
+                    function=Function(
+                        name="write",
+                        parameters={
+                            "type": "object",
+                            "properties": {"content": schema},
+                        },
+                    ),
+                )
+            ]
+            prefix = "<tool_call><function=write><parameter=content>"
+            tail = "</parameter></function></tool_call>"
+            for value in ('中文🙂"\\' * 100, "null", "NULL", "nullable", "\n\nbody\n"):
+                text = prefix + value + tail
+                expected = json.loads(
+                    Qwen3CoderDetector()
+                    .detect_and_parse(text, tools)
+                    .calls[0]
+                    .parameters
+                )
+                for chunk_size in (1, 2, 3, 5, 17, 4096):
+                    with self.subTest(
+                        schema=schema, value=value[:20], chunk_size=chunk_size
+                    ):
+                        detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
+                        parts = []
+                        open_text = prefix + value
+                        for offset in range(0, len(open_text), chunk_size):
+                            parts.extend(
+                                c.parameters
+                                for c in detector.parse_streaming_increment(
+                                    open_text[offset : offset + chunk_size], tools
+                                ).calls
+                            )
+                        if len(value) > 100:
+                            self.assertIn('"content": "', "".join(parts))
+                            self.assertLess(len(detector._buffer), 128)
+                        for offset in range(0, len(tail), chunk_size):
+                            parts.extend(
+                                c.parameters
+                                for c in detector.parse_streaming_increment(
+                                    tail[offset : offset + chunk_size], tools
+                                ).calls
+                            )
+                        self.assertEqual(json.loads("".join(parts)), expected)
+
+    def test_streaming_nonstring_schema_conversion_is_preserved(self):
+        """Array unions and other typed values must never enter the string path."""
+        cases = [
+            (
+                {
+                    "anyOf": [
+                        {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
+                        {"type": "null"},
+                    ]
+                },
+                '["NYC"]',
+                ["NYC"],
+            ),
+            ({"type": ["array", "null"]}, '["NYC"]', ["NYC"]),
+            ({"type": "integer"}, "42", 42),
+            ({"type": "boolean"}, "true", True),
+            ({"type": "object"}, '{"a": [1, 2]}', {"a": [1, 2]}),
+        ]
+        for schema, value, expected in cases:
+            tools = [
+                Tool(
+                    type="function",
+                    function=Function(
+                        name="write",
+                        parameters={
+                            "type": "object",
+                            "properties": {"content": schema},
+                        },
+                    ),
+                )
+            ]
+            text = "<tool_call><function=write><parameter=content>" + value
+            tail = "</parameter></function></tool_call>"
+            for chunk_size in (1, 2, 3, 5, 17, 4096):
+                with self.subTest(schema=schema, chunk_size=chunk_size):
+                    detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
+                    parts = []
+                    for offset in range(0, len(text), chunk_size):
+                        parts.extend(
+                            c.parameters
+                            for c in detector.parse_streaming_increment(
+                                text[offset : offset + chunk_size], tools
+                            ).calls
+                        )
+                    self.assertEqual("".join(parts), "")
+                    parts.extend(
+                        c.parameters
+                        for c in detector.parse_streaming_increment(tail, tools).calls
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(json.loads("".join(parts)), {"content": expected})
+                    parsed = Qwen3CoderDetector().detect_and_parse(text + tail, tools)
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        json.loads(parsed.calls[0].parameters), {"content": expected}
+                    )
+
+    def test_streaming_string_terminators_and_repeated_calls(self):
+        """Split terminators must close only their value and reset the next call."""
+        for terminator in ("</parameter>", "", "</parameter>\n"):
+            text = (
+                "<tool_call><function=write_file><parameter=content>\n\nbody\n"
+                + terminator
+                + "<parameter=count>42</parameter></function></tool_call>"
+                + "<tool_call><function=write_file><parameter=content>null</function></tool_call>"
+            )
+            expected = [
+                json.loads(c.parameters)
+                for c in Qwen3CoderDetector().detect_and_parse(text, self.tools).calls
+            ]
+            for chunk_size in (1, 2, 3, 5, 17, len(text)):
+                with self.subTest(terminator=terminator, chunk_size=chunk_size):
+                    detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
+                    parts = {}
+                    for offset in range(0, len(text), chunk_size):
+                        for call in detector.parse_streaming_increment(
+                            text[offset : offset + chunk_size], self.tools
+                        ).calls:
+                            parts[call.tool_index] = (
+                                parts.get(call.tool_index, "") + call.parameters
+                            )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        [json.loads(parts[k]) for k in sorted(parts)], expected
+                    )
+
+    def test_interrupted_stream_does_not_close_string_parameter(self):
+        detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
+        chunks = [
+            "<tool_call><function=write_file><parameter=content>",
+            "x" * 1000,
+            "y" * 1000,
+        ]
+        fragments = []
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            result = detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, self.tools)
+            fragments.extend(call.parameters for call in result.calls)
+            self.assertLess(len(detector._buffer), 128)
